At a tense Capitol Hill hearing, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. was pressed on a growing measles crisis—and his response said it all.

More than 1,700 cases have already been confirmed in 2026, with lawmakers citing a 675% increase. The hardest-hit communities are those already facing barriers to healthcare.

RFK Jr. dismissed the surge as a “global outbreak” and called the criticism partisan.

But for families affected, this isn’t politics. It’s real.

Video
Watch the full report: piped.video/watch?v=lK78k3sx…

Former FBI agent Dan Brunner: Everybody wants to call this a security failure. I see it the opposite—I think this is a security success.

From what we saw, the suspect wasn’t even close to breaching security. He still would have had to go down two flights of stairs and get through additional secured doors. He didn’t even reach the magnetometers before being stopped.

There were shots fired, and one agent was reportedly struck in a vest. It’s unclear how that occurred, but the key point is this:

You’d think the acting AG would be prioritizing justice after an apparent mass shooting attempt involving top officials in our government, but he seems more focused on getting Donald Trump’s ballroom built—something that has nothing to do with last night’s event.
